reason: Semgrep 1.178.0, the newest release, requires pyjwt~=2.13.0, so the fixed 2.14.0 cannot be installed with it. The flaw makes a JWK set with one malformed RSA key fail to parse; its maintainers describe it as a conditional availability failure, not a signature or claims bypass. Semgrep runs here without a login and never parses a JWK set. Remove this entry when Semgrep allows PyJWT 2.14.0 or later.

Semgrep 1.178.0, the newest release, requires pyjwt~=2.13.0, so the fixed 2.14.0 cannot be installed with it. The flaw lets tokens with unknown key IDs make a server's PyJWKClient refetch its JWKS endpoint on every request, an availability issue for services that validate incoming tokens. Semgrep runs here without a login, validates no incoming tokens and never uses PyJWKClient. Remove this entry when Semgrep allows PyJWT 2.14.0 or later.
